validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE is directly and strongly confirmed, not GEM-derived. The sheet's own first wiki citation (PNGRB/Auth/2-NGPL/BID/KSPL/(17)/2018) resolves to a real, on-topic PRIMARY regulatory document -- I fetched the PDF directly (https://pngrb.gov.in/pdf/ngp/Govt-Authorization/Authorization_2_20032020.pdf) and it is a scanned/image PDF (no extractable text layer, hence the url_verifier false-negative -- see note below), so I OCR'd all 3 pages with tesseract at 300dpi. It is a dated (20.03.2020), signed 'final acceptance' letter from PNGRB's Additional Adviser (Arvind Kumar) to Indian Oil Corporation Limited's Executive Director (Projects), ref PNGRB/Auth/2-NGPL/(17)/2018, subject 'Final acceptance for dedicated natural gas pipeline from Petronet LNG Re-gasification Terminal, Dahej to Indian Oil Corporation Limited's Koyali Refinery'. Body text: 'the system capacity of approx. 106 km length, 16" diameter dedicated natural gas pipeline from Petronet LNG Re-gasification Terminal, Dahej to Indian Oil Corporation Limited's Koyali Refinery is equal to 5.23 MMSCMD* as indicated by Indian Oil Corporation Limited.' This is a genuinely independent, primary-source, GEM-independent origin naming this exact pipeline (not a generic/aggregate citation) and confirming length, diameter, capacity, route and sole ownership all at once. SECOND independent origin: DNA India (2018-03-08 print report, live URL now 403s -- anti-bot -- but a clean Wayback capture from 2018-03-10 verifies OK): '...106-km captive natural gas pipeline from Dahej to Koyali at an estimated cost of Rs315 crore are the other projects to be undertaken by Gujarat Refinery...' -- independently corroborates the 106 km length, the Dahej-to-Koyali route, and is the exact source the wiki page's own infobox cites for its cost figure (Rs315 crore / US$42.6M). THIRD independent origin: India Investment Grid (indiainvestmentgrid.gov.in, a Government of India / DPIIT infrastructure-project portal, project ID 701295, page title 'Dahej-Koyali Refinery Natural Gas Pipeline Project in Vadodara, Bharuch (Gujarat)') -- independently confirms: Sector Oil & Gas / Bulk Material Transportation Pipelines, State Gujarat, Project Start Date 2017-08-03 (consistent with the PNGRB letter noting IOCL's application was dated 02.12.2017), Project Completion Date 2022-02-26, Project Status 'Completion Certificate/COD' (i.e. commercially operational), Promoter/Sponsor Type 'Central PSU' (consistent with IOCL, though the portal does not name the promoter by name in publicly-visible text), and Total Project Cost USD 39.61 mn. Three genuinely independent, GEM-independent origins (a regulator, a national investment portal, and contemporaneous press) all describing the same specific pipeline -- existence is solid, tier high. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is reasonable -- this is a 106 km, 16in, long-distance point-to-point line moving regasified LNG from an import terminal to a refinery, not a field-gathering or local-distribution line. Note the PNGRB letter itself calls it a 'dedicated' pipeline (a REGULATORY-ACCESS category, i.e. not open to third-party common-carrier use) rather than 'transmission' -- but 'dedicated' vs 'common carrier' is an ownership/access axis, orthogonal to GEM's transmission/gathering/distribution PipelineType axis, so no reclassification is warranted; flagging the distinction here so it isn't mistaken for a mismatch. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 35-row India roster. Two other rows also originate at/near Dahej -- P0919/P3298 (Dahej-Vijaipur DVPL-I/II, Dahej to Madhya Pradesh, 770/610 km, owner GAIL not IOCL) and P2212 (Dahej-Uran-Panvel-Dhabhol, Dahej to Maharashtra, 815 km) -- but all three go to entirely different, much more distant destinations under a different owner (GAIL's trunk grid vs. this row's dedicated IOCL refinery feeder). P2210 is a genuinely distinct, short (106 km), dedicated point-to-point line to a specific refinery -- not a relabel or segment double-count of any sibling row. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Indian Oil Corp 100% is confirmed by the PNGRB letter, which is addressed exclusively to IOCL ('this acceptance letter being issued to Indian Oil Corporation Limited is not transferable') and by IIG's 'Central PSU' sponsor category, consistent with (though not verbatim-naming) IOCL. StartLocation/EndLocation (Dahej -> Koyali, Vadodara district, Gujarat) confirmed by all three sources; IIG's own page title names both Vadodara AND Bharuch districts (Dahej itself sits in Bharuch district), matching GEM's EndPrefecture/District=Vadodara for the refinery end. NOTE on url_verifier: the PNGRB authorization PDF is scanned/image-only (no text layer) so url_verifier correctly returns HTTP 200 but 'missing expected' for any text token -- this is a false-negative class (documented for other large/scanned PNGRB PDFs in this project), confirmed here via manual OCR (tesseract, 300dpi, all 3 pages) rather than the automated tool.

validity.researcher_notes: The current SegmentCost value (42,600,000 USD) traces to the wiki page's own citation of the DNA India article, which I independently confirmed via Wayback ('...at an estimated cost of Rs315 crore...' -- Rs315 crore = US$42.6M at the exchange rate used in the wiki's own conversion). This is a pre-construction ESTIMATE published in March 2018, four years before the pipeline's actual 2022 completion. India Investment Grid -- a Government of India project-tracking portal, independent of both DNA India and PNGRB -- lists the SAME completed project (matching name, location, promoter type, and 2022-02-26 completion date) with 'Total Project Cost: USD 39.61 mn', a ~7% LOWER figure. The two numbers are not identical, but a ~7% gap between a 2018 pre-construction estimate and a later as-built/reported actual cost is well within the normal range of project-cost evolution and is not, on its own, evidence that either figure is wrong -- so I am treating this as a caveat rather than a material spec disagreement requiring an existing value to be flagged as an error. Both figures are independently sourced and verified; I am proposing to KEEP citing the DNA article for the existing 42.6M value (since that is what the value actually equals, to the dollar-and-cent conversion) while surfacing the IIG figure here for Update's awareness rather than silently omitting it.
